answer: Every claim passes through a spiral of checks: two neighbours read it, a relic seals it — a signed receipt from a job they actually finished — and a quill copies it into the public record. The desk checks the receipt against the record within a day; a claim with no receipt, or one copied from someone else, is rejected and the identity barred a week. One honest user carries one receipt, but 1,000 fakes would need 1,000 receipts, each from real work. When one operator filed a thousand claims on one stolen receipt, the desk found the same relic number on every one and threw them all out.
